========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, doctor, I'm here because... well, it really all started at work. I’ve been a nursing assistant for a long time, you know, and I know my unit inside and out. I know every single beep, every alarm, every squeak of the wheels on the med carts. I know what the floor sounds like. But lately, things have just been... different. I mean, I'm usually the one who answers the call lights, right? That's a big part of my job, making sure the patients are okay. But it's not just the normal call light sounds anymore. 

I keep hearing these voices. And not just, you know, people talking down at the nurse's station or doctors whispering in the halls. No, they're coming right out of the call-light speaker itself. And the hallway vents, too—especially the big ones right above room 412 and down by the clean utility room. I'll be standing there, and it'll be the middle of the night, completely dead quiet on the floor, not a single soul walking around, and I hear them. 

And they aren't just making noise, they are telling me exactly which patient records have been changed. They just rattle off the information about whose charts have been altered, and I’m telling you, it is as clear as day. I mean, it is as clear as somebody standing right next to me, just like you're sitting here right now! I even asked the charge nurse and the other aides if they heard the speaker going off, or if they heard the vents, and they just look at me with blank stares because nobody else hears it. But I know what I'm hearing. The unit will be perfectly, perfectly quiet, but the voices are just so loud and specific about these records, and it's making it so hard to just do my normal vitals and rounds because I have to stop and listen to them, so... well, I guess that's why they said I needed to come in and talk to you today.

Well, see, it's not that I'm not coherent. I mean, I know exactly what I'm saying, it's just that there is so much information coming at me all at the exact same time, and I have to process it all. So when I try to say it out loud, I guess it might sound like a lot to someone else who isn't keeping up, but to me, it's all completely connected. It's just moving at a million miles an hour and I can't hit the pause button. I just keep flipping from the measurements to the dates to the initials, over and over, because if I don't keep track of it, who will? So yeah, it's hard to express it sometimes just because people can't listen as fast as I'm thinking.

I mean, sure, the voices from the vents and the call lights are a lot to handle, and keeping track of all those changed records takes up so much of my energy, but depressed? A special role? Yes! Yes, exactly, that is exactly what it is. Because think about it, why else would I be the only one putting the pieces together? It’s specifically the wound-care charts. I’ve been looking at them—well, not looking at them like I’m snooping, but when I’m doing my own charting at the end of the shift, I see things. Coding mistakes! Can you believe that? As if a stage three sacral pressure ulcer just magically shrinks by two centimeters in a single shift because of a 'coding mistake.' Please. I've been doing this job too long to buy that. 

But I didn't push it with her, because I realized right then and there exactly what was happening. I can tell they're watching me now. Management, the charge nurses, they are watching exactly what I write in the system. Every single time I log into that computer at the nurse's station, I can feel eyes on me, monitoring my keystrokes, because they know I'm the one who caught it. I'm the one who saw the pattern they were trying to hide with all these fake late entries. So if that's not a mission, I don't know what is. I have to be the one to keep tracking it, because if they know I know, I have to be careful, but I also have to be perfectly accurate so they can't just delete what I've found. I have to stay one step ahead of them.

Not real? How could they possibly not be real? I mean, honestly, Doctor, that is exactly why I'm here in the first place. I'm here because I keep hearing these voices, and I am telling you, they are as real to me as you are sitting across from me right now.

Brenda will just be sitting there two feet away from me, scrolling on her phone or eating a yogurt, completely oblivious, while this voice is giving me step-by-step details from the vents about the chart alterations! 

So when you ask if it's possible they aren't real... I just don't understand how that could be. How could my brain just invent all of that? They are giving me specific, actionable information about the records. I hear them clear as day, even when the unit is completely silent and nobody else seems to care enough to listen.

Problems? Oh, my goodness, Doctor, it has completely turned my life upside down. I mean, it’s just been a complete nightmare. Just the other day—I think it was Thursday, or maybe Wednesday, but I was right in the middle of my shift, right in the middle of getting my vitals for the 400 block, and my supervisor, the same one I told you about who completely ignored my spiral notebook, she actually pulled me off the floor. He's trying to keep our lives running, but I can see how stressed he is, and I just... I can't stop to help him, because if I stop, I'll lose track of the pattern, but it's just ruining everything.

Brenda will just be sitting there two feet away from me, scrolling on her phone or eating a yogurt, completely oblivious, while this voice is giving me step-by-step details from the vents about the chart alterations! \n\nSo when you ask if it's possible they aren't real...
